description: We're AstroByte! A team of three engineering students passionate about programming, technology, and space exploration. We enjoy building software, solving problems, and turning creative ideas into practical solutions. With skills in software development, web technologies, and UI/UX design, we're excited to take on NASA Space Apps Challenge, learn new things, and create something meaningful!
summary: We are the AstroByteX team, and we chose the "Create Health Monitoring Software" challenge. We built AstroCare, a health monitoring platform that helps astronauts keep track of their health during space missions. Living in space comes with unique challenges, including isolation, exposure to space radiation, and limited access to immediate medical support. Astronauts need to monitor different health measurements, but it can be difficult to understand what these numbers mean, notice changes over time, and know when something may need attention. AstroCare lets users record their health measurements and complete daily check-ins about how they feel. It then analyzes this information to show health graphs, highlight unusual readings, and provide alerts and recommendations. This helps astronauts better understand their health, recognize changes that may need attention, and make more informed decisions during their missions.
details:
What it does?

Overview: Shows heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure, body temperature, and blood glucose, with a color-coded overall Health Status.

Daily Check-in: Records sleep, mood, and factors affecting the day, with daily reminders.

Analytics: Interactive graphs over 7 days or a month, with unusual readings highlighted.

Reports: Detailed health assessment with averages, ranges, changes, and practical recommendations.

Alerts: Warnings at two levels (Watch and Outside Range), plus a prominent on-screen alert for serious concerns that explains the issue and the next step.

Extras: Individual accounts, mission day tracking, and support for English, Arabic, and German.

How it works?

The astronaut enters measurements and daily check-ins.

Data is saved to their personal account, building a continuous health record.

AstroCare compares readings with expected ranges and past readings to find unusual values and patterns.

It produces an overall Health Status, or says more data is needed instead of assuming everything is fine.

Results appear in Overview, Analytics, and Reports, with alerts and recommendations explaining what was detected, why it matters, and what to do.
